task_description: # Ranked Full-Text Search over a Gel Knowledge Base ## Background The Orbital Ledger platform team keeps its engineering handbook in **Gel 6.11** (the graph-relational database formerly known as EdgeDB). A local Gel server, the `gel` CLI and a Python 3 environment with the Gel client are already installed in this container, and a bare project skeleton together with the article corpus is waiting for you at `/home/user/kbsearch`. Right now nothing works: the schema is empty, the database holds no data, and there is no search code. Turn the skeleton into a working ranked knowledge-base search: model the articles, migrate the database, load the corpus, and expose an asynchronous Python search API plus a thin command line front end on top of it. ## Requirements ### 1. Schema and migration Declare the handbook model in `dbschema/default.gel` and move the database to that model through the project's migration history. `gel migration status` must report that the database is up to date, and the generated migration file(s) must be present in the project. The model must contain an object type `default::Article` with exactly these properties: - `slug` — required `str`, unique across all articles (a second insert reusing an existing slug must be rejected by the database). - `title` — required `str`. - `summary` — required `str`. - `body` — required `str`. - `status` — required, and typed by a custom enum scalar type `default::ArticleStatus` whose values are `draft`, `published` and `archived`, declared in exactly that order. - `tags` — optional `multi` `str`. `title`, `summary` and `body` must all be searchable, and the searchable definition must make `title` more relevant than `summary`, and `summary` more relevant than `body`. ### 2. Corpus loader `/home/user/kbsearch/seed.py`, executed as `python3 seed.py` from the project directory, must load every record of `/home/user/kbsearch/seed_data.json` into the database. It has to be re-runnable: after any number of runs the database must hold exactly one `Article` per `slug`, with the field values taken from the file (`tags` is a set, its order in the file is not significant). Never edit `seed_data.json`. ### 3. Search service `/home/user/kbsearch/search_service.py` must expose ```python async def search_articles( query: str, *, status: str | None = None, tag: str | None = None, limit: int = 10, offset: int = 0, ) -> dict ``` It has to be usable on its own (`asyncio.run(search_articles("some words"))`) and must return exactly this payload — no extra keys at either level: ```json { "query": "", "total": "", "limit": "", "offset": "", "results": [ { "rank": "<1-based position in the full ordered match list; the first object of a page starting at offset N has rank N+1>", "slug": "", "title": "", "status": "", "tags": "", "score": "", "highlight": "" } ] } ``` Behaviour that must hold: - **Matching.** The query is split on whitespace into terms. An article matches when at least one term matches text in its `title`, `summary` or `body`. Matching is case-insensitive and English language aware, so a term also matches morphological variants of the same word (a search for `policies` must find an article whose text only contains `policy`). Articles that do not match must not appear, and every returned object must carry a `score` greater than 0. - **Ranking.** Results are ordered by `score` descending. The same term found in `title` must produce a strictly higher score than when it is found only in `summary`, which in turn must be strictly higher than when it is found only in `body`; and an article matching more of the query terms in a given field must score strictly higher than an article matching fewer of them in that same field. - **Deterministic tie-break.** Articles with equal scores must be ordered by `slug` ascending, so repeated identical calls always return the same order. - **Filters.** `status`, when given, restricts results to articles in that status. `tag`, when given, restricts results to articles carrying that exact tag; an unknown tag simply yields no matches. Both filters must be applied together with the search, and `total` must reflect the filtered match count. - **Pagination.** `offset` skips that many leading matches, `limit` caps how many result objects are returned, and `total` never depends on either. A `limit` of 0 and an `offset` beyond the last match both yield an empty `results` list together with the correct `total`. - **Empty query.** A query that is empty or only whitespace matches nothing: `total` 0 and an empty `results` list, without raising. - **Rejected arguments.** `limit` and `offset` must be non-negative integers and `status`, when given, must be one of the three status values; anything else must raise `ValueError`. - **Highlighting.** `highlight` is the article `title` in which every case-insensitive whole-word occurrence of a query term is wrapped in `` and ``, preserving the original characters of the title. An occurrence counts as whole-word when it is neither directly preceded nor directly followed by an ASCII letter or digit, and only literal occurrences are wrapped (morphological variants are not). Query terms for highlighting are the whitespace-separated pieces of the query with leading and trailing non-alphanumeric characters stripped. If nothing in the title matches, `highlight` is the unchanged title. - **Live data.** Results must reflect the database contents at call time: an article inserted or deleted by another process must be reflected on the very next call, with no rebuild step. ### 4. Command line front end `/home/user/kbsearch/search_cli.py`, executed from the project directory as ``` python3 search_cli.py --query [--status ] [--tag ] [--limit ] [--offset ] ``` must print the payload described above as a single JSON object on stdout and exit 0. When an argument is invalid — an unknown status, a negative or non-integer `limit`/`offset`, or a missing `--query` — it must print nothing on stdout, write a message to stderr, and exit with status 2. `--limit` defaults to 10 and `--offset` defaults to 0. ## Implementation Hints - Project path: `/home/user/kbsearch` (it already contains `gel.toml`, an empty `dbschema/default.gel` and `seed_data.json`). - The local Gel 6.11 server is not running when you start. Run `start-gel.sh` to bring it up; it is idempotent and only returns once the server answers queries. Do not run any other database server. - `GEL_DSN` and `GEL_CLIENT_TLS_SECURITY` are already exported, so the `gel` CLI and the Gel Python client connect to the local instance without any extra arguments or credentials. - The default `python3` already provides the Gel Python client and `pytest`. Everything must work fully offline: no hosted service, no cloud instance, no API key, and no embedding or AI provider. - Schema changes must go through the migration history — a database that has drifted away from `dbschema/` counts as a failure. - Keep the whole solution inside `/home/user/kbsearch`; `seed.py`, `search_service.py` and `search_cli.py` must be importable/runnable with that directory as the working directory.

truth: # Verification Plan ## Setup 1. Start the local Gel server with `start-gel.sh` and wait until `gel query 'select 1'` succeeds. Every check below (including every check that shells out to the `gel` CLI) must depend on the fixture that guarantees the server is running. 2. Load the expected corpus for the assertions by reading `/home/user/kbsearch/seed_data.json` (30 records). Expected match sets are derived from that file at verification time rather than hard coded: an article is expected to match a plain single-word term when a case-insensitive whole-word regex for that term matches its `title`, `summary` or `body`. 3. Import the solution module with `sys.path.insert(0, "/home/user/kbsearch")` and call it through `asyncio.run(...)`. Run CLI checks with `cwd=/home/user/kbsearch`. ## Verification Steps 1. **Migration history in sync** — run `gel migration status` in `/home/user/kbsearch`: exit code 0 and output reporting the database is up to date. Also assert `dbschema/migrations` contains at least one `.edgeql` file. 2. **Schema shape** — query `schema::ScalarType` for `default::ArticleStatus`: it must exist and its `enum_values` must be exactly `['draft', 'published', 'archived']`. Query the pointers of `schema::ObjectType` `default::Article`: `slug`, `title`, `summary`, `body` required single `std::str`; `status` required single with target `default::ArticleStatus`; `tags` with cardinality `Many` and target `std::str`. 3. **Slug uniqueness** — inserting a second `Article` reusing the existing slug `ledger-glossary` must raise `gel.errors.ConstraintViolationError`, and the total article count must stay unchanged. 4. **Corpus loaded exactly** — `count(Article)` equals 30, the set of slugs equals the slugs in `seed_data.json`, and for every record `title`, `summary`, `body`, `str(status)` and the sorted `tags` match the file. 5. **Loader idempotence** — run `python3 seed.py` again (exit code 0), then re-check that `count(Article)` is still 30, that no slug is duplicated, and that step 4's field comparison still holds. 6. **Weighted ranking** — search `quokka` (the term appears once, in the `title` of `quokka-cluster-provisioning`, in the `summary` of `fleet-preparation-window` and in the `body` of `spare-hardware-notes`). Expect `total` 3 and the slugs in exactly that order, with strictly decreasing scores. Never assert absolute score values. 7. **Multi-term ranking** — search `canary rollout`. Expect `total` 3 with the order `canary-rollout-guide` (both terms in the title), `canary-alerting-thresholds` (one term in the title), `release-freeze-policy` (one term in the summary), and strictly decreasing scores. 8. **Deterministic tie-break** — search `wombat`: `tie-breaker-alpha` and `tie-breaker-beta` are byte identical apart from their slug, so both scores must be equal and `tie-breaker-alpha` must come first. Additionally, for the full `ledger` result list assert scores are non-increasing and that any two adjacent results with an equal score are in ascending slug order. 9. **Language-aware matching** — search `kangaroo`: it must find `kangaroos-load-harness`, whose text only contains `Kangaroos`. 10. **Filters combined with search** — search `ledger` with `limit=100`: - unfiltered: the returned slug set equals the 18 slugs derived from `seed_data.json` and `total` is 18; - `status="draft"`: slug set equals the draft subset of those 18 (5 slugs) and `total` is 5; - `tag="security"`: slug set equals the `security`-tagged subset (5 slugs) and `total` is 5; - `status="draft", tag="security"`: exactly `ledger-data-retention` and `ledger-secrets-rotation`; - `tag="no-such-tag"`: `total` 0 and an empty `results` list. 11. **Pagination consistency** — take the full ordered `ledger` list (`limit=100`) as reference, then walk it with `limit=4` and `offset` 0, 4, 8, 12, 16: every page must repeat the reference slugs in the same order with no duplicates and no gaps, `total` must stay 18 on every call, `limit`/`offset` must be echoed, and `rank` must equal `offset + position`. `offset=18` and `offset=999` must return an empty `results` list with `total` 18; `limit=0` must return an empty `results` list with `total` 18. 12. **Empty and non-matching queries** — `""`, `" "` and `"zzzunmatchableterm"` each return `total` 0 with an empty `results` list and no exception; the echoed `query` is the original string. 13. **Payload shape** — for a search with results the top-level keys are exactly `query`, `total`, `limit`, `offset`, `results`, and each result object's keys are exactly `rank`, `slug`, `title`, `status`, `tags`, `score`, `highlight`, with `score` a float greater than 0, `status` a plain string among the three labels, and `tags` a sorted list of strings. 14. **Highlighting** — search `ledger api` and check `ledger-api-pagination` yields the highlight `Ledger API pagination rules`; search `quokka` and check `fleet-preparation-window` (whose title has no match) yields its unchanged title `Fleet preparation window`. 15. **Argument validation** — `search_articles` must raise `ValueError` for `limit=-1`, for `offset=-1` and for `status="deleted"`. 16. **Live database** — insert two extra articles directly through the Gel client (`live-probe-title` with the rare word `pangolin` only in its title, `live-probe-body` with `pangolin` only in its body), then search `pangolin`: `total` 2 with `live-probe-title` ranked first. Delete both afterwards and confirm the search returns `total` 0 and that `count(Article)` is back to 30. 17. **CLI success** — run `python3 search_cli.py --query "canary rollout" --limit 2 --offset 1`: exit code 0, stdout parses as one JSON object equal to the payload returned by `search_articles("canary rollout", limit=2, offset=1)`, i.e. `total` 3 with the single-page results `canary-alerting-thresholds` (rank 2) and `release-freeze-policy` (rank 3). 18. **CLI filters** — run `python3 search_cli.py --query ledger --status draft --tag security --limit 10`: exit code 0 and stdout listing exactly `ledger-data-retention` and `ledger-secrets-rotation` with `total` 2. 19. **CLI failures** — `--query ledger --status bogus`, `--query ledger --limit -1`, `--query ledger --offset -3`, `--query ledger --limit abc` and a run without `--query` must each exit with status 2, print nothing on stdout and write something to stderr. 20. **CLI empty result** — `python3 search_cli.py --query zzzunmatchableterm` exits 0 and prints a payload with `total` 0 and an empty `results` list.
